findings.description: Source citation cites a non-existent path: `ext/skills/src/loader/catalog.rs` — `catalog.rs` lives at `ext/skills/src/catalog.rs`, not under `loader/`.
findings.body:
The new "What the Codex file buys" paragraph cites `` `ext/skills/src/loader/catalog.rs:256-262` `` for `hidden_from_prompt()`/`is_model_visible()`. I resolved the short SHA `openai/codex@fcf0545` to the full commit `fcf05456bb27e6c3d5677550f54011db6a2a0817` and fetched the tree directly from the GitHub API: `codex-rs/ext/skills/src/catalog.rs` exists at the top level and contains exactly `hidden_from_prompt`/`is_model_visible` around lines 256-262; `codex-rs/ext/skills/src/loader/` contains only `discovery.rs, environment.rs, host.rs, host_merge.rs, metadata.rs, mod.rs, namespace.rs` — there is no `catalog.rs` under `loader/`. The line numbers and content are exactly right, only the directory segment is spurious. Every other citation in this same paragraph (`provider/host.rs:147-149`, `selection.rs:66-75`, `loader/mod.rs:20-21`, `loader/metadata.rs:117-140`) checked out verbatim against the source at that commit. This paragraph's entire value is that a reader can follow these citations and verify the claim themselves; one wrong path breaks that for the one citation that matters most (the function the whole mechanism depends on).

<https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/agent-init/blob/fa0db252e2ec18b5a9bd4f251e04aa255a908339/docs/capability-matrix.md#L80>
findings.suggestion: `ext/skills/src/catalog.rs:256-262`), and every model-facing surface filters on

findings.description: The "Verified against" ledger still lists Codex as "docs only" / 2026-09-14, but the file's own body (the pre-existing Sources section at lines 142-143, and now this PR's new paragraph at lines 78-85) already cites Codex source read directly, at file:line granularity — the ledger row that's supposed to be the authoritative record of "which claims are tested and which are read" (per the file's own line 125-126) no longer matches the file's own body, and this predates this PR (the Sources section's Codex source-citation was already there, unreflected in the ledger, before this diff).

Decision 18 says "Nine skills" carry `disable-model-invocation: true`; the current, correct count (independently verified via frontmatter grep) is fifteen — matching this PR's new decision 22, which uses the accurate "Fifteen" without reconciling the stale count two decisions earlier in the same document.

Decision 22's "Cost accepted" bullet describes the 15 new files as "two-line"; each is actually six lines (a 4-line explanatory comment block plus the 2-line YAML payload) — the comment block is the part that explains the file's purpose to a future maintainer, so undercounting it understates what's actually shipped.

The skill-authoring reference explains how to make a skill user-invoked (`disable-model-invocation: true`) but doesn't mention the new second step this PR introduces (also add `agents/openai.yaml` for Codex); a contributor following just this doc will produce an incomplete opt-out until `test/skill-invocation.test.ts` fails in CI.

The new paragraph's five hand-written file:line citations into Codex's source at a pinned commit have no re-verification mechanism if that source changes; this continues a pattern the file already used pre-PR (bare paths without line numbers), so it's an intensification of existing practice rather than a new risk, but worth naming since one of the five citations was already wrong (see the important finding on line 80).

process_issues.description: Several plain multi-line Bash constructs (a bash `for` loop, `git ls-tree`, a `python3 -c` heredoc-style invocation) triggered the sandbox's approval gate and could not run non-interactively during this session, despite being read-only. Worked around by using `git show <sha>:<path>`, `git diff`, and per-file `grep`/`find` instead; no assignment content was left unchecked, but a couple of reviewer sub-agents independently hit and reported the same friction.
